newsitem.title: USA: Bankrupt Discovery Zone turning to junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: Bankrupt Discovery Zone turning to junk bonds.

text.p: Discovery Zone Inc., the insolvent indoor play centre company, will look to the "junk bond" market to finance its emergence from bankruptcy, according to sources familiar with the transaction.

The sources said the company, which filed for bankruptcy protection 15 months ago, plans to sell $85 million in five-year senior secured notes via Jefferies and Co. Inc. in a private placement toward the end of July.
A hearing on the final bankruptcy plan, which will include details of the financing, has been scheduled for July 18.
Discovery Zone, based in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., operates 208 indoor play centres around the country.
To increase investor interest, the company is also expected to give bondholders an undisclosed amount of equity in the new company in the form of warrants, the sources said.
Proceeds from the offering will be used to pay back a debtor-in-possion facility, administrative fees and expenses and then to finance the company's turaround plan.
The company aims to raise an additional $15 million through the private placment of preferred stock, the sources said.
Company officials declined to comment due to Securities and Exchange Commission disclosure restrictions.
Discovery Zone, which once had a stock market value of $1.3 billion, filed for bankruptcy in March 1996.
After emerging from bankruptcy, Discovery Zone will be controlled by Martin Davis, former chairman of Paramount Communications Inc., and a group of investors.
The group gained control of the company by buying its bank debt at a deep discount.
Last December, Viacom Inc. wrote off its 49 percent investment in Discovery Zone, which it owned through its Blockbuster Entertainment unit. Viacom no longer owns a stake in the company.
